title: Bessent Says AI Industry Must Own Its Risks and Find Solutions
source_used: The Next Web, relaying an Axios interview and Bloomberg (Bloomberg original blocked)
key_facts: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in an Axios interview published Saturday 3 Oct 2026, criticised AI leaders who warn of disaster without offering fixes: 'alarmism without solutions ... that's not leadership'.
He said responsibility for managing AI risk sits with the labs; asked about executives calling for regulation, he said 'then they should slow down'.
He said the US 'cannot lose our lead to the Chinese' and that Chinese models can be '80%, 90% as powerful' as US ones but without guardrails.
Axios also reported the US plans to propose a system for warning China about serious AI incidents.
Bessent discussed AI risks, including rogue agents and misuse for cyber or biological attacks, with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York in September.

Context: in September Amodei, Altman and Musk called for slowing work on the most advanced models; Trump has called AI doom warnings a hoax and said last week he does not want an AI safety deal with China.
quote_evidence: "This alarmism without solutions by some of the AI community, that's not leadership," Bessent said, as Bloomberg reported.
"It is the people at the labs who have to accept responsibility, and I agree with that," he said.
Asked about executives calling for regulation, he replied: "Well, then they should slow down."
why_it_matters_hint: The Treasury chief confirms the administration's line: no new federal rules, the labs carry the risk, and competition with China comes first.
notes: Bloomberg (pool source) blocked by a robot check. The remarks were made to Axios; Bloomberg and The Next Web relayed them, so Axios is the first reporter. The Axios URL was not available; url points to the TNW page where the text was read.
